description.short_caption: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain showing hyperintense lesions.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial T2-weighted MRI image of the brain at a higher axial cut. The image demonstrates hyperintense lesions in the white matter, particularly in the right hemisphere, suggestive of possible demyelination, edema, or infection. The ventricles and midline structures appear symmetric, and there is no obvious midline shift.
visible_findings: hyperintense lesions in the white matter

Case_04033/figure1.jpg.source_caption: MRI scan of the brain, axial T2-weighted image.

description.short_caption: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain showing cortical and subcortical structures.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial T2-weighted MRI image of the brain. The cortical and subcortical structures are well visualized, with hyperintense signal in the cerebrospinal fluid spaces and gray matter differentiation. There is no obvious mass effect, midline shift, or focal lesion visible in this image. The sulci and gyri appear prominent, suggesting possible cortical atrophy.
visible_findings: no visible mass effect or midline shift
